data.name: Shauryaar
data.gender_notes: Shauryaar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Shaurya', meaning 'rule', 'authority', or 'dominion'. In Hindu mythology, Shaurya is an attribute of various gods, representing their supreme power and sovereignty. The name Shauryaar carries the meaning “Rule, Authority, Dominion” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Shauryaar usually hope their child will grow to embody rule, authority, dominion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the inner strength and moral authority to lead and govern.
data.etymology: Shauryaar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rule, Authority, Dominion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shauryaar total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shauryaar carries a strong sense of power, command, and leadership in Hindu culture. It is often associated with individuals or deities who possess great authority, strength, and status. Shauryaar is a name that inspires respect, admiration, and loyalty from those around it.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Shauryaar represents the divine power and sovereignty of God or the gods. It is a reminder of their all-encompassing authority and control over the universe. The name encourages those who bear it to embody the qualities of supreme power, courage, and righteousness, and strive to rule their own lives with wisdom, compassion, and integrity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shauryaar signifies the embodiment of valor and courage. It is a name for those who fearlessly face challenges and uphold truth and righteousness. The wisdom of a lion and the courage of a tiger resonate within those called Shauryaar.

vedic_reference.note: शौर्य (Shoury) is a synonym of वीर्य (Veery), which is a common attribute of various deities and heroes in Hindu mythology.

historical_references.reference: The Mahabharata describes Shaurya as the name of a powerful and righteous king, the ruler of Haihayas in the ancient Indian subcontinent. He is also known as Kuru-Shaurya, as he is a descendant of the Kuru dynasty.

Shaurya is also mentioned in Jain and Buddhist texts as a prince of Magadha, who renounced his kingdom and became an ascetic. According to these texts, he was a contemporary of Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Jain and Buddhist texts
